entry.title: How We Give AI Agents Long-Term Memory Without Blowing the Budget
entry.summary: Giving agents long-term memory is hard: context windows are limited, storing every raw message is expensive, and retrieval has to be both fast and relevant. entry.title: Designing Zero-Trust CI/CD Pipelines with GitHub Actions and AWS
entry.summary:
TL;DR GitHub OIDC + AWS STS to authenticate using identity, not passwords. For years, CI/CD pipelines have relied on static cloud credentials: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Even when stored in secret managers, these credentials create long-lived attack surfaces. Secrets accidentally committed to GitHub Leaked through logs or misconfigured pipelines Keys valid for months or years Manual rotation (often forgotten) A leaked AWS key in a public repo can be exploited within minutes by automated bots. This is why the industry is moving toward identity-based security. Traditional security answers: “Do you have the key?” Modern security asks: “Who are you, and can you prove it right now?” This is the foundation of workload identity federation.
